title: An Axon Is a State, Not a Stamp

scenes.tts: Cut a neuron's axon close to the cell body, and one of its dendrites can grow out as a new axon. Cut the axon farther away, and the old axon simply regrows. So an axon is not a permanent label. What decides which process becomes the axon, and what keeps it that way?
scenes.visual: A polarized neuron is cut near the body and a dendrite turns into the axon; the neuron is rebuilt, cut farther out, and the old axon regrows; a question closes the scene.
scenes.narration: Cut a neuron's axon close to the cell body, and one of its dendrites can grow out as a new axon. Cut the axon farther away, and the old axon simply regrows. So an axon is not a permanent label. What decides which process becomes the axon, and what keeps it that way?

scenes.tts: Start in a dish. A rat hippocampal neuron grows several short neurites, and they all look alike. After a day or two, one neurite starts to grow much faster than the rest. That neurite becomes the axon. A neurite tends to win once it is about ten micrometres longer than the others. The choice behaves like a race.
scenes.caption: Start in a dish. A rat hippocampal neuron grows several short neurites, and they all look alike. After a day or two, one neurite starts to grow much faster than the rest. That neurite becomes the axon. A neurite tends to win once it is about 10 micrometres longer than the others. The choice behaves like a race.
scenes.visual: Five equal neurites on a round cell; a bar chart of their lengths; one neurite pulls ahead, turns yellow and becomes the axon.
scenes.narration: Start in a dish. A rat hippocampal neuron grows several short neurites, and they all look alike. After a day or two, one neurite starts to grow much faster than the rest. That neurite becomes the axon. A neurite tends to win once it is about 10 micrometres longer than the others. The choice behaves like a race.

scenes.tts: A race with one winner needs two kinds of feedback. Positive feedback in the leader makes it grow faster the more it grows. A lipid called P I P 3 builds up at its tip. Blocking P I 3 kinase is reported to stop any neurite from becoming an axon. Negative feedback holds the others back. How it does that is less settled.
scenes.caption: A race with one winner needs two kinds of feedback. Positive feedback in the leader makes it grow faster the more it grows. A lipid called PIP3 builds up at its tip. Blocking PI3-kinase is reported to stop any neurite from becoming an axon. Negative feedback holds the others back. How it does that is less settled.
scenes.visual: The leader gets a growth loop and green PIP3 dots at its tip; a crossed-out PI3-kinase chip shows no axon; red bars with a question mark sit on the other neurites.
scenes.narration: A race with one winner needs two kinds of feedback. Positive feedback in the leader makes it grow faster the more it grows. A lipid called PIP3 builds up at its tip. Blocking PI3-kinase is reported to stop any neurite from becoming an axon. Negative feedback holds the others back. How it does that is less settled.

scenes.tts: Look at the growth cone, the moving tip of the leader. Its actin network is looser than in its siblings. Loosened actin is proposed to let microtubules push in, and the microtubules there are more stable. Loosen the actin in a chosen neurite, or stabilize its microtubules, and that neurite can become the axon.
scenes.visual: Two large growth cones side by side: dense actin and short microtubules in the sibling, loose actin and deep microtubules in the leader; the sibling then loosens and takes the leader's look.
scenes.narration: Look at the growth cone, the moving tip of the leader. Its actin network is looser than in its siblings. Loosened actin is proposed to let microtubules push in, and the microtubules there are more stable. Loosen the actin in a chosen neurite, or stabilize its microtubules, and that neurite can become the axon.

scenes.tts: Once chosen, the axon has to be held. Near the cell body, a scaffold called ankyrin G builds the axon initial segment. It works as a gate. Lower ankyrin G in a mature neuron, and the segment falls apart. A dendrite protein called M A P 2 spreads into the axon. The axon begins to look like a dendrite.
scenes.caption: Once chosen, the axon has to be held. Near the cell body, a scaffold called ankyrin G builds the axon initial segment. It works as a gate. Lower ankyrin G in a mature neuron, and the segment falls apart. A dendrite protein called MAP2 spreads into the axon. The axon begins to look like a dendrite.
scenes.visual: A mature neuron with a purple initial segment; blue MAP2 dots stay in the dendrites; ankyrin G is removed, the segment dissolves, the dots flow into the axon and it turns dendrite-like.
scenes.narration: Once chosen, the axon has to be held. Near the cell body, a scaffold called ankyrin G builds the axon initial segment. It works as a gate. Lower ankyrin G in a mature neuron, and the segment falls apart. A dendrite protein called MAP2 spreads into the axon. The axon begins to look like a dendrite.

scenes.tts: Now return to the cut. Leave a stump shorter than thirty-five micrometres, and no process is clearly ahead. It is like the first race again, and a dendrite can win it. Leave a longer stump, and the old axon regrows. Keep this rule. An axon is a state the cell holds. If enough of it is lost, that state can pass to another process.

scenes.visual: Neuron with a length bar chart: after a short-stump cut the bars are level and a dendrite wins; after a long-stump cut the stump bar is already tallest and regrows.
